summary: Tianshu Zhu works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA at Northwest University and a PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington, later holding posts at Northwest University, Shaanxi History Museum, Ohio State, and Korea University.

Tilak Kariyawasam is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as head of the Department of Pali and Buddhist Studies at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1993) and as Dean of the Graduate School at International Buddhist College (attested 2014).

Tilmann Vetter (1937–2012) was a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Vienna (~1957–1962) studying under Erich Heintel and Erich Frauwallner, and was a professor at Leiden University from ~1976 to 2002.

Timothy Hugh Barrett is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied at the University of Cambridge and Yale University. He taught at Cambridge (attested 1981) and became a professor at SOAS University of London in 1986.

Timothy Lenz specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed graduate studies at the University of Washington under Richard G. Salomon and Collett Cox (attested 1999) and held academic posts there, attested as a professor in 2017.

Timothy Lubin is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD from Columbia University in 1994. He has held positions at Washington and Lee University (attested 2012–2020) and collaborated on the DHARMA project.
Tina Rasmussen is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. She completed her MA under the supervision of Christian K. Wedemeyer and also studied under traditional teacher Pa-Auk Sayadaw.

Tirumalai Krishnamacharya (1888–1989) worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, the University of Mysore, and under Ramamohana Brahmachari, later teaching at Maharaja's Sanskrit College, Mysore (1931) and Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College (~1953–1958).

Tissa Rajapatirana (1933–2021) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the Australian National University (1966–1974) under Jan Willem de Jong. He later worked in ANU's Department of South Asian and Buddhist Studies (attested 1988).

Tista Biswas is an Indology scholar who studied under doctoral supervisor Subuddhi Charan Goswami and holds the post of Sir William Jones Research Fellow in Sanskritic Studies at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).
Tiziana Pontillo is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She studied at the University of Cagliari in 2016 and held a post there in 2022.
Todd A. Gibson works in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under György Kara and earned a PhD from Indiana University Bloomington (attested 1991).

Todd Thornton Lewis works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Columbia University under Theodore Riccardi Jr., Alex Wayman, and others, and served as Murray Distinguished Professor of Arts and Humanities at the College of the Holy Cross.

Tokan Tada (1890–1967) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sera Monastery (1913–1923). He held appointments at the University of Tokyo (1924), Tohoku University (1925), and the Toyo Bunko (1956).
Toke Lindegaard Knudsen is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied under Kim Plofker and completed his doctorate under David Pingree in 2008.

Tokio Takata is a Sinology, linguistics, and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Kyoto University and the EHESS, and served as professor at Kyoto University (1997–2014) and Fudan University (2016–2022).

Tokugen Sakai (1912–1996) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University, Kyoto University, and under Kodo Sawaki. He was later an emeritus professor at Komazawa University (1949–1987) and taught at Eihei-ji (1977–1987).

Tokuno Oda (1860–1911) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fukui Prefectural Normal School, Otani University, and under Junjirō Takakusu and Gaju Ikehara. He held teaching posts at Fukui Chugakko (1879–1882) and Toyo University.

Tokuryu Yamauchi (1890–1982) was a philosophy and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and Freiburg under Nishida, Husserl, and Heidegger. He held professorships at Hitotsubashi University, Kyoto University, and Ryukoku University.
Tom De Rauw specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies under Ann Heirman and holds an AAP post at Ghent University (attested 2026).
